receptor_A.expressed_in_muscle: yes — PMID:17123512 confirms ErbB receptor expression in skeletal muscle stem cells; HPA RNA consensus shows medium expression in skeletal muscle

receptor_B.expressed_in_muscle: yes — EGFR is ubiquitously expressed; HPA shows medium RNA expression in skeletal muscle; known to be expressed in satellite cells and myofibers

step_1.geometry_asymmetry: low — |ECD_A - ECD_B| = 9 aa (630 vs 621); nearly identical ECD lengths
step_1.forced_proximity_agonism_defensible: yes — both are ErbB family RTKs that naturally heterodimerize; forced proximity via GS_med linker will drive transphosphorylation at the intracellular kinase domains. The near-identical ECD lengths (9 aa difference) mean the ICDs will be positioned at nearly the same distance from the membrane, enabling symmetric transphosphorylation.

step_2.structure_tier_A: PDB_experimental — ERBB2 ECD: 1N8Z, 1S78; multiple high-resolution structures available
step_2.structure_tier_B: PDB_experimental — EGFR ECD: 1IVO, 1NQL, 2GS6; extensive structural coverage
step_2.natural_dimerization: yes — ERBB2 and EGFR are known obligate heterodimerization partners (Reactome: R-HSA-1963589). ERBB2 is the preferred dimerization partner for all other ErbB receptors. However, forced-proximity via the novokine linker locks the dimer in a specific geometry that differs from ligand-induced dimerization, creating biased signaling.
step_2.novelty_flag: moderate — natural heterodimer exists, but forced-proximity geometry biases the output away from the natural ligand-induced signaling pattern

step_3a.notes: Adaptor classification based on Reactome signaling pathways for ERBB2:EGFR heterodimers (R-HSA-1227986, R-HSA-177929) and known phosphotyrosine docking sites
transphosphorylation_adaptors: SHC1 — binds pY sites on both ERBB2 and EGFR; amplified under forced proximity as both kinases phosphorylate SHC1 simultaneously
GRB2 — directly binds pY1068/pY1086 on EGFR and pY1139/pY1196 on ERBB2; enhanced by transphosphorylation creating more docking sites
SOS1 — recruited by GRB2; RAS-GEF activity drives MAPK cascade; transphosphorylation creates more GRB2-SOS1 recruitment platforms
GAB1 — scaffold that binds GRB2 and recruits PI3K; both ERBB2 and EGFR phosphorylate GAB1, amplified under forced proximity
PIK3R1 (p85 regulatory subunit of PI3K) — binds pY sites on ERBB2 (pY1196) and via GAB1; transphosphorylation enhances PI3K recruitment
cis_adaptors: SRC — phosphorylates EGFR at Y845 and ERBB2 at Y877; this is a cis event that occurs even without forced proximity
PTK6 — binds ERBB2 and is activated; can occur in cis in natural dimers
excluded_adaptors: PLCG1 — binds pY992 on EGFR and pY1196 on ERBB2 via its SH2 domains. Under forced-proximity with GS_med (~30 Å), the co-clustered ICDs create steric constraints that prevent PLCG1 from productively docking. This is the same exclusion mechanism seen in H2F (ERBB2-FGFR1), where PLCG1 is sterically excluded. The ~9 aa ECD symmetry here is tighter than H2F, but the GS_med linker still constrains the ICD geometry enough to exclude PLCG1's large multi-domain structure.
GRB7 — binds ERBB2 pY1139; its RA-PH domain requires specific membrane orientation that may be disrupted by the forced co-clustering geometry

step_3b.notes: Pathway cassettes derived from Reactome analysis of adaptors recruited via transphosphorylation
biased_pathways: MAPK/ERK signaling (R-HSA-5673001) — via SHC1→GRB2→SOS1→RAS→RAF→MEK→ERK cascade; the primary transphosphorylation-driven output
PI3K/AKT signaling (R-HSA-1257604) — via GAB1→PIK3R1→PIP3→AKT; enhanced by transphosphorylation creating more GAB1 docking sites
mTOR signaling — downstream of AKT; promotes protein synthesis and cell growth
Cell cycle progression — via ERK-dependent MYC and CCND1 transcription
excluded_pathways: PLCγ/Ca²⁺ signaling (R-HSA-212718) — excluded due to PLCG1 steric exclusion
PKC signaling downstream of PLCγ — secondary exclusion

step_3c.notes: TF→target mapping based on MAPK/ERK and PI3K/AKT downstream transcription factors (ELK1, SRF, MYC, FOS, JUN, ETS family, FOXO family)
step_3c.predicted_up_rationale: MAPK/ERK and PI3K/AKT activation drives expression of proliferation, survival, and growth genes
step_3c.predicted_down_rationale: Suppression of senescence, inflammation, and atrophy programs via AKT-mediated FOXO inhibition and reduced inflammatory signaling

step_3d.notes: BioGRID ORCS screens show ERBB2 and EGFR are fitness genes in multiple cancer cell lines (essentiality screens). No muscle-specific CRISPR screens available. EGFR is a well-validated drug target with extensive genetic perturbation data.

step_4.notes: Gene lists assembled from MAPK/ERK and PI3K/AKT transcriptional targets, filtered for relevance to muscle rejuvenation (young-enriched = up, aged-enriched = down)

mechanism_narrative: ERBB2-EGFR forced-proximity novokine with GS_med linker (~30 Å) drives transphosphorylation between the two ErbB family RTKs, which have nearly identical ECD lengths (630 vs 621 aa, asymmetry = 9 aa). This symmetric geometry enables robust SHC1-GRB2-SOS1 and GAB1-PI3K adaptor recruitment, amplifying MAPK/ERK and PI3K/AKT signaling. PLCG1 is sterically excluded due to the constrained ICD geometry imposed by the GS_med linker, suppressing the PLCγ/Ca²⁺ branch. The biased output upregulates proliferation/survival genes (MYC, CCND1, DUSP6, ETV4/5) and downregulates senescence/inflammatory markers (TXNIP, IL32, S100A4, LGALS3), shifting aged muscle toward a younger transcriptional phenotype. Unlike H2F (ERBB2-FGFR1), this ERBB2-EGFR pair has minimal ECD asymmetry, making it a more symmetric forced-proximity dimer with potentially stronger MAPK output but less dramatic pathway biasing than the highly asymmetric H2F.
